ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: SW — Trophy Craft
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
WYYYSCHOKK_FANG_PENDANT_1 (owner's direct spec, 2026-09-13, verbatim): "add this awesome concept to the game for the Wildsteam/Blackstar/ Deep Tribe factions, as they all have a concept of respected hunting: Wyyyschokk fangs on a tribal pendant showing the bravery of the person. These should have social consequences for being worn by implying the person is quite brave (with those factions), and be a trade good elsewhere on planet regardless."
Ships the mechanism, owns no campaign data:
1. `RSW_WyyyschokkFang` (ThingDef, ResourceBase) — a stackable trophy resource, small marketValue on its own. A patch (`RSW_TrophyCraft_WyyyschokkFangDrop.xml`) attaches it as a butcherProducts entry on the third-party `Wyyyschokk` ThingDef (`mlie.starwarsanimalcollection`, Star Wars Animal Collection — confirmed by the same species-ownership search `RimMandrake: SW — Shokk`'s About.xml already recorded: there is no RUT_/RSW_-owned Wyyyschokk def anywhere in this repo, only PatchOperations against the donor's). A patch that matches nothing logs nothing, so this mod loads fine with or without that donor installed — it simply never drops fangs without it. 2. `RSW_Apparel_FangPendant` (ThingDef, apparel) — crafted at a hand tailor bench from fangs + cloth (the "textile cord"), low work, no research prerequisite (tribal tech level). Worn on a brand-new `RSW_Neck` ApparelLayerDef, bodyPartGroup `Neck` only: 🔴 **VERIFIED, not guessed** — the live def dump (232 ThingDefs covering `Neck`, captured against the ~630-mod list) shows 153 of them share the vanilla `Middle` layer while covering `Neck` (shirts, vests, robes), so a Neck-only accessory on `Middle` would silently block wearing a robe, a vest or most tribal wraps at the same time — exactly the silent collision this item's own doctrine warns about. Reusing a third-party layer (`Jewelry`'s or `Romance On The Rim`'s `Accessories`) would trade that collision for a soft dependency on a mod that can be removed out from under it. Owning a brand-new layer used by nothing else is the only zero-collision, zero-dependency answer, so that is what ships: the pendant can always be worn with anything else in the 630-mod list. 3. `RSW_TrophyCraft_ObserverBraveFang` (ThoughtDef, social, worker `RSW_ThoughtWorker_ObserverFactionApparel`) — a plain, Harmony-free `ThoughtWorker` (spec option (a); the ideoligion precept route is explicitly rejected — precept budget is FactionDef-fixed, so a named precept would be design register, not mechanism). It reads its target apparel defName and its list of "regards this as brave" faction defNames from a `RSW_FactionApparelThoughtExtension` `DefModExtension` on the ThoughtDef. **This mod ships that extension EMPTY** — RimStarWars tier does not know the Utinni campaign's factions. `RimUtinni Patches` (`mandrake.rut.patches`) wires in the real three via `WyyyschokkFangPendantFactions.xml`, keeping campaign data in the RUT tier where it belongs. +opinion magnitude is a Mod Settings slider, default ON. 4. Trade: `RSW_Apparel_FangPendant` carries `tradeTags: ExoticMisc` (the same tag `Jewelry_Necklace` uses to sell everywhere) and a real `MarketValue`, so any settlement or trader buys it — no faction check gates the sale. The Bazaar's worldTag weighting could later make hunting-tribe settlements pay MORE for it; that seam is noted, nothing Bazaar-side is built here.
**Live quicktest owed** beyond this build's offline `validate_patch.py` pass: butcher a Wyyyschokk, craft the pendant, spawn a Wildsteam/Pirate/TribeCivil observer and an unlisted one, confirm the opinion delta appears only for the listed factions, confirm the pendant sells to a vanilla trader. See `infrastructure/state/items/WYYYSCHOKK_FANG_PENDANT_1.md`.
